Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. The hero from Afghanistan's last match, Fazalhaq Farooqi to bowl first. Finn Allen and Devon Conway to open.
...THE CHASE...

Right then! This is just above-par score in this conditions. The dew has started to kick in a bit! Afghanistan think they have enough and it does look enough but New Zealand are coming with a long tail here. A good powerplay could put New Zealand on the front foot. A fascinating second half coming up. Stay tuned.

Afghanistan would have loved another 10-15 runs here but this is a formidable score on a pitch which is not easy to bat on. Afghanistan were asked to bat first and the lady luck was with the Asian team as their openers made most of the chances given and builded a 103-run stand. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz targeted a couple of bowlers and scored at a good rate but at multiple times where Afghanistan went a few overs without a boundary and if you see the overall score, and the runs scored apart from top three, there is not much. It was hard for batters to come in and hammer it away.

Afghanistan's man of the moment, Rahmanullah Gurbaz is in for a chat. He says that considering the bowling they have, this is a good total and he is happy with it. Shares that it was not easy at the start against the spinners. Adds that their plan was to play safely against Santner and charge other bowlers. Tells that the pitch is not easy and hopes that his side can bowl and field well.

A tale of two halves really for the Kiwis. They will be happy with how they ended with the ball but boy, that was some school-match stuff from New Zealand. There was so much action in the powerplay, firstly luck wasn't on their side but on the contrasting side, they didn't take their chances. A dropped catch, a run out chance, an LBW decision overturned, then Lockie Ferguson trapped Rahmanullah Gurbaz in the 8th over but they didn't take the review as they thought there was an edge, close to the halfway mark Kane Williamson dropped Rahmanullah Gurbaz again. It was all going downhill for them but somehow New Zealand kept Afghanistan at bay! They made it hard for Afghanistan to score runs in the second half and that helped New Zealand to stay in the game but still, we feel the momentum is with the Afghan side.

Wow! How rare is this? Just 3 runs off the final over in a T20 game. Sensational stuff from Trent Boult. This is full and angling into the left-hander from over the wicket, Najibullah Zadran looks to play at it but gets an inside edge that goes down to deep fine leg. Just a single off it then. Afghanistan finish with 159 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely shot! Santner slows it up and goes full, on middle, Ibrahim Zadran presses forward and goes inside out over cover for a classy boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: Given LBW but Ibrahim Zadran has succesfully overturned it! New Zealand's delight is short-lived. Fires it in with the angle, on a good length, Ibrahim Zadran misses out on the sweep and gets rapped on the back pad. The finger goes up and Ibrahim takes the review after having a word with Gurbaz. There is nothing on UltraEdge but the ball is going over the leg stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mitchell Santner to Ibrahim Zadran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz knocks it down to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, no! New Zealand are not helping themselves in the field here! Rahmanullah Gurbaz gets away with it. Santner drops it short, on off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz shuffles and steers it to short third. Sets off for the single but gets sent back by his partner. Gurbaz has to put in the dive and the dive isn't going to save him as the short third fielder is quick to release the throw but the keeper, Devon Conway fails to hold on and spills an easy chance.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A single to end the over! Could have had a wicket as well! Length and on the pads, Rahmanullah Gurbaz nudges it to mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Matt Henry to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Calls for two and gets it easily! Length and on middle, Rahmanullah Gurbaz tucks with soft hands to mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Matt Henry to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, Ibrahim Zadran pushes it to mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! This should have been taken! Finn Allen is the culprit! Not the start the Kiwis were looking for! Short in length and on middle, Ibrahim Zadran pulls it flat to deep square leg where Finn Allen runs to his right and tries to take near his chest but drops a standard catch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Has Lockie Ferguson misjudged there? Was in the air for a while! Shorter and angling on the hips. Zadran looks to pull but mistimes it to short fine leg. Lockie Ferguson first goes back and then puts a late shift to go for the catch. Ends up taking it on a bounce.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and on leg. Zadran stays back and tries to defend but miscues it on the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! How did the bails not come off? Afghanistan are riding their luck! There was definitely a sound, Gurbaz is lucky to survive. Santner bowls it quick, full and on leg. Rahmanullah Gurbaz uses his feet and swings across but misses. The ball deflects off the leg stump and it goes past the mitts of Conway and to the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYES! Santner tails it on the pads. Rahmanullah Gurbaz misses his flick and it goes off the pads to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 2 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted full and on middle, Rahmanullah Gurbaz digs it out back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and on middle, Ibrahim Zadran drives it to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mitchell Santner to Ibrahim Zadran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mitchell Santner bowls it quick and this one holds a bit, on the middle and Rahmanullah Gurbaz backs away and knocks it to covers for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mitchell Santner tosses it up and tails it on middle and leg, slides on a lot. Rahmanullah Gurbaz prods to defend but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal for LBW but the finger stays down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mitchell Santner to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for early spin as Mitchell Santner comes into the attack.
Just a single now! Short in length and on the hips. Rahmanullah Gurbaz pulls it to short fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air and wide of Trent Boult! Ibrahim Zadran has not yet hit his strides here. Tad fuller and around off. Ibrahim Zadran punches on the up and to the left of Boult, it falls short of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Trent Boult to Ibrahim Zadran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! This one shapes in late and stays down. A length ball from around the wicket and on middle and leg. Rahmanullah Gurbaz misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. Easily, going down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Top nut from Boult! Just keeps changing his lines and lengths here. A length ball, outside off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz goes back to cut but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fails to time here! Shorter and on middle, Ibrahim Zadran miscues his pull shot to square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Trent Boult to Ibrahim Zadran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Trent Boult comes around the wicket and slants it full and around off, Ibrahim Zadran pushes it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Trent Boult to Ibrahim Zadran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Expensive over from Matt Henry but he has the Afghani openers on their toes all through. A good length delivery, around off. Rahmanullah Gurbaz looks to defend but outside edges it just to the left of short third man and it races away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Matt Henry to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Dropped? No, given as a leg bye! Short in length and on middle, wobbled seam and came with an angle. Ibrahim Zadran bends his back to ramp it over but goes off the arm to the right of the keeper. Devon Conway fails to hold on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Much more in control! This will help his confidence a lot. Pitches it up on middle, Ibrahim Zadran flicks on the up and over mid-wicket for a boundary. Afghanistan off to a bright start.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Off the edge! Third time lucky you reckon here. Touch fuller and comes with the angle on leg. Ibrahim Zadran opens his stance to heave but inside edges it well past the keeper and to fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A huge shout for LBW but that was straying down. Again, Ibrahim Zadran is beaten for the pace. Twice now. Full and on the pads, Ibrahim Zadran looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Matt Henry serves it on a length and around off, Ibrahim Zadran is beaten for pace, tries to punch but splices his shot through point for a couple of runs. He is off the mark now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Matt Henry to Ibrahim Zadran, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Matt Henry.
A length ball, on middle, shapes in late here. Rahmanullah Gurbaz has his stumps covered as he blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Teasing delivery! A length ball, outside off, holds its line. Rahmanullah Gurbaz gets his head down to defend but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz taps it in front of point.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Two runs and Afghanistan are underway! Half-a-chance here! Trent Boult dishes a low full toss as he tries to find some swing, this is on middle, Rahmanullah Gurbaz flicks on the up but in the gap through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Past the outside edge! Expect Trent Boult to make it move in the start! A length ball, angled across Rahmanullah Gurbaz who tries to defend but does so inside the line.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Trent Boult to Rahmanullah Gurbaz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems and are all set for the action to commence. The two umpires make their way out to the middle and the players of New Zealand join them. It will be the talented pair of Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to open the innings for Afghanistan. Trent Boult is at the top of his mark and he is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the first ball in this crucial Group C clash but before that, Kane Williamson and Rashid Khan will lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

PITCH REPORT - Katey Martin is pitchside. She starts by saying that a nice breeze is blowing across the ground. Informs that pitch number 2 will be used for this game, resulting in an 84-metre long straight boundary with 77 metres and 70 metres being the square boundaries. Simon Doull joins her and says that since back-to-back games are going to be played at this venue, the ground staff have left a good amount of grass. Feels that the batters will be tested on this surface which will assist pacers and there will be a bit of spin as well.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan says they are happy to bat first, tells they want to play good cricket and get used to the conditions as quickly as possible. Tells they had a couple of rests day, they recovered after the last match and are ready for this big game. Informs Mujeeb Ur Rahman is out due to an injury and Noor Ahmad is back. Mentions Mujeeb Ur Rahman is struggling with the same injury and it is hard to understand how much time it will take.

The captain of New Zealand, Kane Williamson says that they will bowl first. States that they want to make first use of the fresh surface and feels that there might be some dew around later. Tells that the preparation has been different as compared to other teams but they have trained well over the past week and they are looking forward to this game. Informs that Tim Southee, Rachin Ravindra, Ish Sodhi and James Neesham miss out.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Gulbadin Naib, Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Najibullah Zadran, Karim Janat, Rashid Khan (C), Noor Ahmad (In for Mujeeb Ur Rahman), Naveen-ul-Haq, Fazalhaq Farooqi.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Kane Williamson (C), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and will BOWL.

It won’t be easy for them though as they are facing a tough assignment against Afghanistan who have adapted to the conditions pretty well. Where teams are struggling to score even 150, the Asian team scored 183 against Uganda, Farooqi was the hero with the ball as he scalped five wickets. Afghanistan, who in the last couple of years would be called underdogs are termed favourites to go all the way this year. That’s the leap they have taken and definitely, this is the contest you don’t want to miss. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Hello and welcome to the action in Group C where New Zealand will take on Afghanistan. Mostly all the teams have played a match or two but the Kiwis start their campaign today and that could be a positive sign for them. We have seen how the pitches have been different from what we are used to see and the Kiwis would have got an idea or two of how the conditions are and could get things going right away.

New Zealand will face Afghanistan in the 14th game of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024. New Zealand is a strong contender for the title and will aim to start their campaign strongly. Afghanistan, having defeated Uganda, will look to perform well but has a poor record against New Zealand. Kane Williamson's team, despite not playing warmup games due to key players being involved in the Indian T20 League, and will aim to make a strong start in the tournament and secure their first points. With one of the strongest squads in the competition, they will be determined to meet high expectations. They will rely on an explosive opening partnership of Devon Conway and Finn Allen, followed by experienced players like Kane Williamson, Daryl Mitchell, and Mark Chapman in the middle order. The team's good finishers, Glenn Phillips, James Neesham, and Mitchell Santner, are expected to contribute in the lower order. The Kiwis side possesses a strong bowling attack as well, led by Trent Boult and Tim Southee, with Mitchell Santner and Ish Sodhi utilizing the pitch conditions. Overall, the team's depth in batting and bowling makes them a formidable opponent in the competition. Rashid Khan's team, on the other hand, has had a strong start in the tournament, with a convincing win over Uganda by 125 runs. Both batsmen and bowlers executed their plans effectively in the previous game. As they face a tougher challenge ahead, Rashid Khan will emphasize the importance of maintaining momentum and securing another victory. Their openers, Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran's impressive 154-run partnership had set a solid foundation for the team in their previous game. The middle order, featuring Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, and Gulbadin Naib, is expected to contribute significantly. Power hitters Azmatullah Omarzai and Rashid Khan add depth to the batting lineup. The bowling unit, led by Fazalhaq Farooqi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman, aims for early breakthroughs. Rashid Khan plays a key role in the middle overs alongside Naveen-ul-Haq, supported by Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, and Gulbadin Naib in a formidable bowling attack. It remains to be seen if Afghanistan can overcome the odds and secure a victory.
